title: concurrent-primer-sandwich-runner and lightweight sparse-kernel telemetry sink
author: Aisha Khatri
description:
Motivation: long-tail occupancy and cross-request primer interference are hard to reproduce with single-session runners. This PR introduces a Concurrent Primer Sandwich workload runner (concurrent pairs of short primer + target sequences) that stresses KV cache churn, packing/steady-state transitions, and small-microburst coalescing. It also ships a lightweight sparse-kernel telemetry sink that records per-kernel occupancy samples and a compact events stream for offline attribution.

What changed (summary): added a new runner binary (bench/primer_sandwich_runner) that can orchestrate N concurrent primer+target sessions with configurable primer overlap, interleaving patterns, and sequence-length distributions. Added instrumentation hooks that emit sparse kernel occupancy samples to telemetry/sinks/sparse_kernel_sink.go, and a small exporter that writes a compact NDJSON events stream for downstream profilers.

Checklist:
- [x] New runner with deterministic RNG seed and replay mode
- [x] Sparse telemetry sink + unit tests
- [x] CI bench workflow integration (bench/ci/benchmarks.yml)
- [x] Documentation + example configs (docs/bench/primer-sandwich.md)
- [x] Manual verification on a small GPU cluster

How to run locally (examples):
- warmup + single run: ./bin/primer_sandwich_runner --concurrency=16 --primer-len-mean=64 --target-len-mean=128 --seed=42 --telemetry=sparse:./out/events.ndjson
- replay: ./bin/primer_sandwich_runner --replay=out/trace-20241112.json

Design notes: the "sandwich" term refers to each actor executing a short primer, then a target request, then optionally a primer again to simulate inter-request priming. The concurrent mode interleaves many such actors with configurable offsets; this reproduces spent KV slots and eviction churn patterns observed in production traces. The sparse telemetry sink intentionally samples kernel occupancy rather than streaming full traces to keep storage and CI bandwidth low. Sample format is an NDJSON event per sample: {"ts":..., "gpu":0, "kernel":"matmul_fp16", "occupancy":0.43, "active_warps":128}

Commits (high-level):
- 1st commit: add runner skeleton, deterministic session scheduler, CLI flags
- 2nd commit: implement primer/target orchestrator, seed-based replay, and examples
- 3rd commit: add sparse kernel telemetry sink, NDJSON exporter, and unit tests
- 4th commit: CI integration and docs

Changed files (high-level):
- bench/cmd/primer_sandwich_runner/main.go
- bench/internal/scheduler/concurrent_scheduler.go
- bench/internal/session/primer_session.go
- telemetry/sinks/sparse_kernel_sink.go
- telemetry/sinks/sparse_kernel_sink_test.go
- docs/bench/primer-sandwich.md
- bench/ci/benchmarks.yml
- examples/bench/primer-sandwich/example-config.yaml
- Makefile (bench target)

Small illustrative snippet (from concurrent_scheduler.go):
"""
// scheduleLoop advances actor ticks and emits start/stop events deterministically
for tick := 0; tick < cfg.Steps; tick++ {
    for _, actor := range actors {
        actor.Advance(tick)
        if actor.ShouldRunNow(tick) {
            dispatch(actor.Step())
        }
    }
}
"""

Testing and CI: The bench CI workflow runs a small-scale smoke run on a single GPU VM and validates NDJSON telemetry format with the unit tests. An earlier run failed flakily due to a goroutine leak reported by Linnea; fixed in commit 3 by adding context cancellation and a bounded worker pool. Final CI run: all checks green; bench smoke + unit tests + linters passed.

Performance notes: On a 4-GPU test cluster with concurrency=128 and primer-target overlap=0.6 we observed a 12% increase in tail p99 latency compared to uniform sequence runners, and a 7% uplift in kernel occupancy variance. Those numbers are captured in artifacts/out/bench-20241112-summary.json linked in the Linear ticket.

Backward compatibility: runner defaults are non-invasive (single-actor mode matches prior single-runner behavior). Telemetry sink is pluggable behind the existing telemetry registry and disabled by default. No breaking API changes.

Related: Linear ENG-1021 (investigate primer interference), ENG-1087 (sparse telemetry spec). References to prior bench artifacts and a small sample trace are included in the docs.
